card.name: Inside split medical terms
card.fires_on: The middle piece of a medical term split into parts, such as 'ure' in sulfonylurea, 'ysis' in tumor lysis, and 'ary' in laryngeal. It fires where the word is unfinished.

modes.label: Sulfonylurea
modes.description: The 'ure' piece inside sulfonylurea(s) in interaction or hypoglycemia text.
modes.example: Patients Receiving Sulfonylureas or Insulin: Sulfonyl<<ure>>a agents or insulin may cause hypog

modes.label: Tumor lysis
modes.description: The 'ysis' piece after 'Tumor l' in the syndrome heading or warning text.
modes.example: 5.8 Tumor Lysis Syndrome Tumor l<<ysis>> syndrome has been reported with Bortez

modes.label: Laryngeal
modes.description: The 'ary' piece in laryngeal edema after angioedema.
modes.example: Angioedema associated with l<<ary>>ngeal edema can be fatal.

card.writes: It mostly promotes odd name-ending pieces, so it has no clear medical output effect.
card.plain: It lights up in the middle of a long medical word that is cut into pieces, like sulfonylurea or tumor lysis.
